correctness.rationale: For all n>=5 the induced disconnected triples partition into a cone A and ball B=Delta({1,n-1})*boundary Delta({2,...,n-2}). The exact intersection is the (n-4)-skeleton of B with two free codimension-one faces excluded. Collapsing their distinct top simplices yields contractible B-prime, with n-5 remaining top cells relative to the intersection, forcing a free integral top homology group. Attaching only top cells preserves lower homotopy, and the Hurewicz-Whitehead argument yields a wedge of spheres. A and B are contractible with cofibration intersection, so their union is the suspension. The n=5 endpoint is handled by the complete collapse. Eight independent finite enumerations support the combinatorial partition and mod-two ranks, and are not mistaken for an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural topological invariant responds maximally differently to the two edge orbits of the classical wheel: the intact and rim-fault cut complexes are contractible, whereas a single hub-spoke fault creates n-5 independent top-dimensional integral homotopy generators for every n>=6. The exact infinite-family classification follows from a structural ball-and-cone decomposition and explains the phase change, rather than reporting arbitrary small numeric increments.
